tool_input.command:
cd <repo>
bd create --title="fix(daemon): unconfigured daemon.json should load zero commands, not all commands unsigned" --type=bug --priority=2 --description "$(cat <<'EOF'
DES-035 (PR #252) wired VerifySignature into beadle-daemon's command loader,
but deliberately preserved legacy behavior when daemon.json is absent:
resolveDaemonOwnerKeyID returns ("", true) for a missing config file, and
loadDaemonCommands then calls daemon.LoadCommands with an empty ownerKeyID,
which disables signature checking and loads every command file in
~/.punt-labs/beadle/commands/ unsigned -- the exact pre-DES-035 posture.

This contradicts the "zero agent authority" design invariant
(docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): "Every action is meant to require a GPG-signed
instruction from the owner." Today that's true only for an operator who
has deliberately configured daemon.json -- the out-of-the-box default is
still "run anything dropped in the commands directory, no signature
required." Operator ruling (2026-08-30, this bead's origin conversation):
fix this -- flip the default so an unconfigured daemon loads NO commands
at all, rather than falling back to unsigned execution.

Scope:
- cmd/beadle-daemon/main.go's resolveDaemonOwnerKeyID: the
  errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) branch currently returns ("", true)
  (loadCommandsEnabled=true, unchanged legacy behavior). Change it to
  return ("", false) -- loadDaemonCommands already treats
  loadCommandsEnabled=false as "command loading disabled entirely,
  daemon.LoadCommands is never called" (this exact code path already
  exists and is tested for the misconfigured case; this bead makes the
  unconfigured case use the same path).
- This is a real, deliberate behavior change for any existing deployment
  that has command files but no daemon.json: those commands will stop
  loading. That's the point -- update docs/wire-verifysignature.md (DES-035),
  DESIGN.md's DES-035 ADR, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's "Zero agent authority"
  bullet, docs/artifacts/trust-model-explainer.html, and CLAUDE.md's "What
  Beadle Is" section (all touched by beadle-iru/PR #252-254) to describe
  the new default: no daemon.json means zero commands load, not unsigned
  commands load.
- CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased, flagged as a breaking behavior change
  for anyone relying on the unsigned-by-default posture.
- Update/add tests: cmd/beadle-daemon/main_test.go's
  TestResolveDaemonOwnerKeyID_MissingConfigIsSilent currently asserts
  keyID=="" with no Error log for the absent-file case -- that assertion
  on the log stays the same (still silent, still the "expected" case), but
  a new assertion is needed on the second return value (loadCommandsEnabled
  should now be false, not true), and internal/daemon/command_test.go's
  disabled-verification subtest needs a sibling covering "absent config ->
  zero commands loaded" to match the new behavior.
- Real-binary verification per the WORKFLOW.md gate: rerun this session's
  three-scenario check (unconfigured, misconfigured, valid) against the
  built beadle-daemon binary and confirm the unconfigured scenario now
  shows count=0 with no commands loaded, not count=1.

Follows the same mission workflow as the original DES-035 wiring
(beadle-iru): dispatch to bwk, evaluated by djb, full local review pass,
real-binary verification before merge.
EOF
)"

cd <repo>
bd create --title="feat(daemon): beadle init/sign tooling for recipe (command) files" --type=feature --priority=3 --description "$(cat <<'EOF'
DES-035 (beadle-iru, PR #252) wired VerifySignature into beadle-daemon's
command loader, gated on daemon.json's owner_handle/owner_gpg_key_id
(the recipe "authorizer" key, per beadle-4ul's pending rename). Once
beadle-kua flips the default to "no daemon.json means zero commands
load," there is no first-class way for an operator to actually produce a
signed recipe file -- they'd have to hand-construct a GPG detached
signature over internal/daemon.CanonicalCommandBytes' exact YAML
re-serialization (Signature field cleared) themselves.

Scope: a `beadle sign` (or similar) CLI subcommand that takes a command
YAML file, computes CanonicalCommandBytes, signs it with a key the
operator selects (their own default GPG key, or one named by flag/config),
and writes the signature back into the file's `signature` field. Consider
also a `beadle init` step (or an extension of the existing `doctor`/
`status` commands) that walks an operator through configuring daemon.json
for the first time.

Referenced as a known gap in prfaq.tex's Feature Appendix and
docs/artifacts/trust-model-explainer.html ("no beadle init/sign onboarding
flow yet"). Not scoped in beadle-iru/DES-035 -- that work only implemented
and wired verification, not signing tooling.
EOF
)"
echo "---"
bd create --title="feat(daemon): implement the tamperproof audit log invariant" --type=feature --priority=3 --description "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Design Invariants section states: "Audit log is
tamperproof. Append-only, GPG-signed entries. Only the owner can clear the
log." No code implements this anywhere in the repo -- confirmed during
DES-035 design work (beadle-iru) via docs/audit-beadle.tex's docs-map
correction: that .tex is a CLI/UX compliance report, not an audit-log
design, and there is no other design doc or implementation to point to.

This is a real gap between a stated security invariant and actual system
behavior: nothing currently records, append-only or otherwise, what
GPG-signed commands the daemon has executed, when, or on whose
authorization. Scope: design (an AuditSink interface was sketched as a
forward-compatible seam in docs/wire-verifysignature.md's DES-035 design
but not implemented) and implement an append-only, GPG-signed audit log
that records at minimum: which recipe ran, the triggering message's
sender and trust level, and the outcome. Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's
invariant bullet once real, not aspirational.
EOF
)"
echo "---"
bd create --title="feat(daemon): implement LLMPlanner so trusted+permitted email content becomes the plan" --type=feature --priority=3 --description "$(cat <<'EOF'
internal/daemon/planner.go defines an LLMPlanner type alongside the
active RulePlanner, but LLMPlanner.Plan is an unimplemented stub
(Plan(_, _, _) returns nothing). Today the daemon's only planner in
production use is RulePlanner, which pattern-matches an email's
subject+body against a small set of hardcoded regexes (one rule,
"(?i)summarize|summary", is hardcoded directly in cmd/beadle-daemon/
main.go's runCmd) to pick a command name and fixed args -- the email's
actual content never becomes a prompt, it only selects among a tiny fixed
menu.

This is the real gap behind the design goal (confirmed in conversation,
2026-08-30, during beadle-iru's trust-model discussion): "the inbound
email from a trusted and verified party is an LLM prompt -- that's the
goal even." beadle-email's /inbox skill already realizes this goal for
the interactive/session-driven path (trusted+permitted content becomes
something an agent reasons about freely). beadle-daemon's unattended path
does not -- it can only ever run one of a fixed, pre-signed set of
recipes, chosen by a hardcoded regex, never a plan derived from the
email's own content.

Scope: implement LLMPlanner.Plan to build a CommandCall plan from message
content, respecting the same trust ladder + rwx checks already enforced
before Plan is ever called (per internal/daemon/handler.go's OnNewMail).
Design question worth resolving explicitly before implementation: does an
LLM-derived plan need its own additional authorization step (since it is
no longer just "pick a pre-signed recipe," but "decide what recipe(s) and
what args to run"), or is trust+permission+recipe-signature sufficient
because the plan can still only ever invoke pre-signed recipes with
LLM-chosen args? That composition question is exactly the kind of
substantive design decision that needs operator ratification before
dispatching an implementation mission, per WORKFLOW.md's design gate.
EOF
)"
